title: Feedback tier catalogue and sprint fragments
body:
Quick summary:
- Goal: compact, prioritized catalogue of customer asks (high-level -> micro-probes) that product and engineering can pick from for the next two sprints. This is intentionally skimmy — think sprint-ready fragments not full specs.
- Tone: operational, cost-aware. Try to surface the smallest demoable change that addresses a real customer pain.

Top recurring signals observed (sorted by frequency & urgency):
1) Latency spikes for multi-turn chat with long KV cache retention (esp. enterprise customers with long user histories). Multiple tickets mention 95th p99 regressions on sequences > 2k tokens.
2) Confusion about model fallbacks and observable routing when Dedicated pools are saturated — customers see different tokens/costs when we route to a quantized variant.
3) Embedding stability/consistency across model upgrades — search relevance shifted after a redeploy for one customer. They ask for stable embed hashes or migration hooks.
4) Billing surprise from occasional over-batching during high-concurrency bursts — they want clearer per-route cost attribution and an option to cap batch size.

Representative customer vignettes (anonymized):
- Vignette A (fintech startup): "We saw a sudden spike in latency during end-of-day batch queries; our users experienced timeouts. Can you guarantee tail latency or provide a low-variance config?" Outcome desired: SLA-pinned policy or a low-latency routing tier.
- Vignette B (healthcare client): "When you switched to model-v2 the embeddings drifted and our patient-matching recall dropped. We need a way to compare embeddings before flipping traffic." Outcome desired: small eval harness + canary metrics for embedding drift.
- Vignette C (marketplace): "Cost increased because our items query started getting batched into larger batches than expected. We need predictable per-request cost and the ability to disable aggressive batching for a route." Outcome desired: route-level batching controls + cost preview.

Consolidated feature requests (fragments, not full PRD):
A. Route-level batching cap (low-effort; platform): config param on routes: max_batch_tokens and max_batch_requests. Default: current heuristic. UI: toggle + numeric cap. Quick probe: add cap to 2 pilot routes for 2 weeks and measure per-token unit cost delta. Owner: Platform Eng. Est effort: 3 dev-days.

B. Embedding migration harness (medium effort; product+applied-ml): lightweight job that computes sample embed-set for a customer's dataset against candidate model versions, returns recall/delta and sample nearest-neighbor diffs. Deliverable: one-click compare in Console for Dedicated/Hosted customers. Quick probe: manual notebook run for 2 customers and share findings. Owner: Applied ML. Est effort: 2 wks for MVP.

C. Low-variance latency tier (larger effort; eng-runtime + Dedicated): reserve small dedicated pool with smaller batching window and pre-warmed KV caches to reduce 95/99 tails for targeted routes. Deliverable: launch alpha for 1 customer on Dedicated. Probe: simulated load test vs current pool. Owner: Serving Runtime + SRE. Est effort: 6-8 wks.

D. Routing transparency + fallback audit logs (small): make routing decisions visible in trace (model id, reason for fallback). Deliverable: trace field and a Console view for last-30-days. Quick probe: add field to existing trace proto, enable for 5 customers. Owner: Observability. Est effort: 1 week.

E. Per-route cost preview (medium): estimate cost-per-request given route config (batch caps, quantization profile, sequence length distribution). UI: preview panel and exportable estimate. Probe: prototype the estimator in a notebook with two sample routes. Owner: Optimize/Product. Est effort: 3 wks.

Priority heuristics (how we ranked the fragments):
- Escalation frequency in CS tickets x customer ARR impact (coarse buckets)
- Implementation effort (T-shirt sizing)
- Measurable signal that we can capture within 2 weeks: telemetry, trace or metric delta
- Risk of regression to other customers (prefer isolated config toggles)

Priority score examples (0-10):
- Route-level batching cap: 8 (high impact, low effort)
- Routing transparency: 7 (low effort, high trust impact)
- Embedding harness: 7 (higher effort, prevents regressions)
- Low-variance latency tier: 5 (high impact but heavy infra investment)
- Per-route cost preview: 6 (medium effort, reduces billing surprises)

Low-effort probes we can ship in the next 2 sprints (1–2 engineers each):
- Add routing_reason to traces and a Console toggle (Observability)
- Implement route-level max_batch_requests flag and launch to 3 customers (Platform Eng)
- Internal notebook: run embedding diff for two sample datasets and document heuristics for acceptable drift (Applied ML)
- Small documentation update and CS-run checklist for model upgrades (DX + CS) — include rollback checklist, sample queries to verify embeddings and latencies.

Open questions & risks:
- Will route-level caps meaningfully increase per-token cost for customers who rely on batching? (need simulated runs)
- Embedding drift detection: what threshold = "actionable"? Is cosine delta enough or do we need downstream recall metric?
- Can Dedicated customers tolerate extra config knobs without increased support load?
- Privacy/data policy: some customers cannot run sample embed probe on production data. Need a privacy-safe sampling protocol.

Owners & next steps (practical plan):
- This week (owners):
  - Diego Morales: implement trace field and add to debug traces for two routes (ETA 2025-02-05)
  - Priya Patel: spin up notebook for embedding diff on 2 customers and schedule readout (ETA 2025-02-12)
  - Maya Chen (me): draft customer-facing explainer and CS checklist for model upgrades (ETA 2025-01-29)
- Sprint 1 (next): route-level batching cap prototype + Console toggle (Platform Eng, 2 devs)
- Sprint 2: run embedding harness manual tests, build estimator prototype for per-route cost preview

Notes to self / meeting talking points for product sync:
- Emphasize small wins that reduce immediate pain (batch caps, routing transparency) over ambitious infra plumbs.
- Flag the low-variance latency tier as a separate strategic workstream — don't block sprint picks on it.
- Ask SRE for cost modeling of smaller pools; include a simple delta table for unit cost vs latency.

Links & refs (internal):
- Linear: CS-412, CS-437, CS-441 (embedding complaints, latency spikes)
- GH PR: runtime#1784 (kv cache TTL work-in-progress)
- Notebook (internal): drive://shared_drives/customer-success/emb-diff-notebook-2025-01-15 (ask Priya for access)

Misc scribbles / unresolved ideas:
- Could we add a temporary "preview routing" mode that shows customers where a request would go without actually routing? Low risk, good for trust-building.
- Consider an "embed-stability" flag for customers who want deterministic hashing across model minor-updates (may require model packaging constraints).

Footer: this doc is intentionally short — treat as pick-list for PM/Eng grooming. If you want one of the fragments turned into a draft PRD, mark it with +PRD and assign to Product.
